I've been playing FIFA since 94', and FIFA has changed drastically until 2006 (when first touch was first introduced). Since then, it's been a cluster of "code & fix". If you're wondering if FIFA is better that PES, it's not. FIFA does indeed have the licenses and obviously the ridiculous ultimate team card gimmick, but in no way, shape, or form is it better (gameplay-wise) than PES. What FIFA does have on PES is Pro Clubs (where you control a single player, or 11v11 players on a field). Apparently, PES does have some sort of league that exists for 11v11, but I'm not sure if it's the same calibre as FIFA's Pro Clubs. In short, PES is way better than FIFA.

As I've mentioned, I'm going to focus this review on the [b]Pro Clubs[/b] aspect - perhaps the only redeeming quality of FIFA. I'm not done ripping on FIFA yet, so let explain why it's NOT better than PES. In PES, the players actually move. They are actively looking to support the player and aren't standing around like a bunch of pylons. FIFA is notorious for having weird (and sometimes often) glitches where the goalie runs over the ball, a defender and goalie collide, switching to a defender makes them stop (further putting a forward on a break-away), and the list goes on. I don't know a single FIFA player that doesn't lose their shit when playing the game. Lots of new swearwords are created, but I don't think you want your game to be known for that.

[b]Pro Clubs[/b]  is a different story. The fact that you can play with your friends and control a single player is amazing. When a player comes together and people are actually moving, it's an amazing experience. The switching problem doesn't exist as you're stuck with your created player. The game goes even further allowing you customize your team (to a point. They probably did this so people don't make extremely whacky players). The one issue that bugs me is that FIFA doesn't seem to realize that players often switch and move positions on the pitch. For example, if I'm a CAM and a friend of mine is a CDM, we can often make runs and switch the position. I allow him to go up sometimes and I'll cover back - simple soccer/football logic no? Well, FIFA will punish you for being out of position (even the slightest bit). For newbies, I do like the fact they hinted at who to mark (and therefore, bring up your score). The scoring system is pretty weird though; I'll get minus marks for playing my position and sometimes a minor bump for scoring a goal. FIFA eh?

Now for you people that play and (unfortunately) support Ultimate Team (unless I guess you own EA stocks), I feel bad for you. Get out of that, because it is truly a gambling addiction. I've seen myself and many friends get dragged into the sub-game and the sub-culture of UT. I've seen people drop stacks of money on virtual cards, and yes to each their own, but it ends up with them being quite sad about it years later. If you're going to play - sure. If you start spending in UT, it's not going to guarantee you'll always win (as heard from voices of rage over discord). I don't know how many more EA games you'll need to buy (or coins for that matter too) until they fix problems they've had for years now. 

Graphics and visuals? Meh, you know the deal with them by now. Sounds and music, ma! The game did have some bangers, maybe I'm just too old to get with the new hippity hop. 
Go support Pro Clubs and go push for Pro Clubs. FIFA could be a decently competitive game if this was possible. Selfishly, I do want more people online so I match quicker on PC (crossplay not available... seriously it's 2021), but I also want to see a better gaming option avialable as well. 11v11 is absolutely mad and there is something about playing with other gamers. Why do I love soccer? Because it's a team game. Wouldn't that magic on the field translate to our screens?

Knowing EA... nawh. Bring in that cash cow labelled UT and keep milking till it has no more. I don't blame them for it; people got to make money. People also overwork themselves sick and often do the jobs of what should be more then one person. This isn't about that though, it's about [b]Pro Clubs[/b] ... and the ONLY reason why  I gave it a thumbs up (just in case you're wondering why).

I'm not going to rate this one and I'm not going to make that wonderful grading table that I usually do. If you buy this, ensure it's on sale and you have a few buddies to play [b]Pro Clubs[/b] with.

With over ten thousand hours spent in FIFA Ultimate Team (FUT, for short) in the last seven years, at a suggestion from a very naughty Czech boy, I decided to record my thoughts on this mode.

[h3][b][i]Polarizing[/i][/b][/h3]
Every journey begins somewhere, and this one, for yours truly, starts with [i]FIFA 14[/i]. FUT back then wasn't really [i]broke[/i] friendly. You had to go through an insane grind only to get a semi-decent team, or, well, you know, shell out for some FIFA Points. There were alternatives, but EA didn't approve of them - [b]pink slips[/b] (putting your player on the line in a PvP wager match) and [b]coin sellers[/b]. FIFA YouTubers and coin sellers, name a more iconic duo. Anyway, very little to do outside of playing Divisions and winning Division 1 for a measly 15k coins, which then shrunk to maybe 8k after expenses - contracts and fitness for your squad. 

EA attempted to bolster the fun in FUT by adding the [b]Draft[/b] in [i]FIFA 16[/i]. After the initial honeymoon phase, it was left by the road and forgotten, mainly because it had an entry fee you had to pay. I love it and play it regularly now, but back then, earning the entry fee of 15k wasn't easy as it is now. 

Fast forward a bit, and [i]FIFA 17[/i] brings what I consider the pillars of FUT today. That year introduced [b]FUT Champions[/b], a PvP weekly competition that made FIFA into an E-sports powerhouse for EA, and [b]Squad Building Challenges[/b], a fun distraction for the players that had the potential to make you a massive profit. Players were now being rewarded by simply playing the game, offered fun SBC challenges they could complete for rewards, and we saw the birth of trading, thanks to these SBCs. All in all, it saw FUT shift from heavily P2W to [i]broke[/i] friendly.

https://steamcommunity.com/sharedfiles/filedetails/?id=2551690040

FUT is packed to the brim with stuff to do. If you don't like online PvP, there is an offline "rip-off" of FUT Champs - [b]Squad Battles[/b] introduced in [i]FIFA 18[/i]. You face random 42 squads taken from other players, with difficulty impacting the points each win nets you. The ranking system is identical to that of FUT Champs, but instead of wins, it uses the number of points earned to rank you. The rewards are also scaled back compared to FUT Champs. Still, it's effortless to reach Elite 1 rank and get around 30k coins and some great packs. There is also an offline version of the Draft, which I found very underwhelming, but I also consider Draft ripe for a makeover. The rewards shouldn't be random, instead, it should be transparent about what rewards we get, like in other game modes. Winning in the finals should, at least, give a Draft Token (free Draft entry) and better packs than basic Gold Packs.

Besides improving the offline experience, those seeking [i]schadenfreude[/i] didn't have much incentive to play anything besides FUT Champs. Well, [i]FIFA 19[/i] sought to change that. The old, god awful, Divisions received a massive overhaul. Dubbed [b]Division Rivals[/b], we got a game mode that didn't feel like a waste of time to play. It's divided into 10 divisions, with each having 6 ranks and excellent rewards for you to choose from, to add even more sweat to your sweaty squad. Promotions or relegations to higher/lower divisions also received a rework. Now, with each win, sometimes a draw, you earn points that go into three pools - your rank in your current division, your progress towards a promotion to the higher division and your progress towards a FUT Champions entry fee. A loss, obviously, hinders your progress, but only for division promotion, as you still get points that help you reach a higher rank in the current division and for the FUT Champions entry fee. Before, it was just a lazy copy of the Online Seasons outside of FUT, and it was abysmal in rewarding you. Division 1 "rewarded" you with 15k coins, and only if you win it. Now you can choose 80k coins, as one of three possible rewards, for reaching rank 1 in division 1. Do you want to know what division has 15k as a reward now? Division 10, rank 3.

https://steamcommunity.com/sharedfiles/filedetails/?id=2551095659

Since it's hip to have a battle pass now, EA also introduces its own version in [i]FIFA 20[/i] in the form of [b]seasons.[/b] They last a month, have 30 levels, with plenty of objectives for you to do each week. Each season has two spots that give you an option to select one out of three special player cards - the first is at level 15 and the other at level 30, as you may have guessed already. While you'll mainly farm XP for the "battle pass" goodies, there are usually also player objectives that can net you some fantastic players, by simply grinding out a couple of games in Squad Battles. But EA has blessed us with something great - [b]Icon Swap[/b], an event that lasts two seasons. There are multiple of them throughout the year, and they add special SBCs - [b]Icon Swap SBCs[/b], that require specific cards - [b]Icon Swap Players[/b], if you wish to reap their rewards. You can earn these cards by completing objectives in each of the two seasons, but each season has its own set, and you can't "go back" and do those you missed. So time is of the essence (something ill come back to later). The rewards for these SBCs are great; You can get either an Icon (one of many on offer), a pack with a guaranteed Icon player, a min rating guaranteed pack, or some of the more rare packs, like the Jumbo Rare Player Pack (24 players, all Gold, all rare).

https://steamcommunity.com/sharedfiles/filedetails/?id=2551111258

Sadly, this year hasn't seen any new additions to FUT that give you a wider range of opportunities to earn coins and players. The most notable change is online co-op improvements. Now you can team up with your friend and earn rewards simultaneously in Division Rivals and Squad Battles. I hope they consider bringing us a version of FUT Champs with co-op in mind and let us play Draft in online co-op, not just local co-op. Besides this, we can now personalize our very own Stadium, and a recent feature put out - Preview packs. I do hope they go forward with them, and they become standard from [i]FIFA 22[/i] onwards. It allows you to see what you can get in a pack before paying. BUT! If you don't like the pack, a 24h cooldown must pass before another preview. If we are going to be completely honest about FIFA 21, it is the textbook definition of a love-hate relationship. Bringing the franchise back to the Steam platform was a huge deal for PC players, but EA managed to leave a very bitter taste in the community's mouth almost immediately.

Let us address the elephant in the room that caused the massive wave of negative reviews: the PC version of FIFA 21 was a direct port of the older generation consoles. PC players were completely denied the next-gen graphics, animations, and engine upgrades that the PS5 and Xbox Series X received. Paying full price for what was essentially an outdated version of the game felt like a massive slap in the face to a community with high-end hardware.

On the pitch, the gameplay is incredibly polarizing. If you love high-scoring, fast-paced chaotic games, you might actually enjoy this. The attacking AI is aggressive, and attackers make smart, creative runs. However, the defending is practically non-existent. Defenders often feel like they are ice skating, tackles bounce right back to the attackers, and the midfield frequently just stands around watching the action. The infamous scripting and dynamic difficulty adjustment are as obvious as ever, leading to those controller-breaking moments where you just know the game has decided you are going to concede a goal in the 90th minute no matter what you do.

Career Mode actually saw some much-needed improvements in this edition, like the interactive match simulation and detailed player development plans. This was a massive breath of fresh air for offline players who felt ignored for years. But as always, the core focus of the game is Ultimate Team. It remains an incredibly addictive, highly engaging mode that is heavily bogged down by aggressive microtransactions, gambling mechanics, and a frustrating pay-to-win structure.

The objective truth? If you only play offline Career Mode and can grab it for a few dollars on a massive sale, the offline improvements make it decent. But as a competitive multiplayer game at full price, it is a frustrating, heavily monetized experience that treated the PC community as second-class citizens.

Not the greatest in the terms of gameplay, but the physics are quite good and ball movement is improved as well, graphica are same as the last installment too.

Gameplay has actually been improved from the previous editions, the movements feel much better (once you get used to the change). Communication with players is better and the position training feature is a huge improvement. The first very big improvement to the game in maybe 5-6 years.

What ruins the game for me:
- Ultimate team, adding skillmoves, useless career mode features (e.g. training) is prioritised instead of improving gameplay. It is a football game, in my opinion gameplay should be number 1 concern.
- The career mode transfers are still totally rubbish and unrealistic like each year.
- The non-player controlled AI defending is absolutely rubbish this year. Central midfielders just stand still, and dont mark any opponents. I guess youre supposed to control all players at once ?? 
- Most ball touch animations look too unrealistic and silly.
- Player speed difference is over-exaggerated which results in slow players are more or less useless.

The minimum expected from an EA game, but it is very poor by any other standards.

The gameplay has changed without any change in quality compared to the previous game. EA did realise that there were issues in attacking play, which is good. Their solution of absolutely nullifying any sort of defensive play, not so much. Ultimate team, being the only really competitive game mode enhances the gameplay issues much more than any other one. With less unnatural and overpowered players in seasons the gameplay feels a lot less like rabid dog running around the pitch with chimpanzees trying to defend your goal. But it's still showing there as well. Career mode has had some changes and improvements taking many of the elements of football manager, but the computer AI is way too weak to pose any sort of competition for anyone whose played the game before. With this the actual "playing" element  of career mode has become very boring, not good. Volta, basically, street football was surprisingly decent this year. The different environments, the in game commentary and soundtrack all added a very nice touch and with different available players such as boxing star AJ made the game mode feel very arcadesque, which it is supposed to feel like. With very different gameplay to the regular game it somewhat complements the mode without really bringing any sort of substance or pull to play, still a good breath of fresh air. The new gameplay elements do not seem to work as poorly with Pro Clubs, since you and your friends can actually use players  defensively. Even with only some minor changes being the "party mode" of FIFA this is the most enjoyable game mode.

I would seriously not recommend anyone buying the game if your main purpose would be to play Ultimate Team, if you're really interested in any other game mode, buy it at half price.
